item.title: Jonathan Gannon reveals how often Packers prepare for Micah Parsons’ return
item.description: The Green Bay Packers could soon get a major boost on defense, with Micah Parsons potentially returning to practice this week. The star pass rusher has spent months recovering from surgery and working toward a return to the field. Defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon has now shared his thoughts on the possibility of having Parsons back with the unit and how frequently he prepares for his return. How often since he got here has Jonathan Gannon game planned for when Micah Parsons returns? “Every day.” pic.twitter.com/Cr5ArOtFX2 — Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) November 3, 2026 “Every day,” remarked the Packers defensive coordinator. Parsons has been out since suffering a torn ACL late in the 2025 NFL season. His recovery has kept him away from the field for several months, with Green Bay yet to announce when he might be ready to play again. However, his progress has brought him closer to returning. The Packers are now working toward taking him off the Physically Unable to Perform list, which would mark another important step in his rehabilitation. When will Micah Parsons return for the Green Bay Packers? Green Bay Packers defensive end Micah Parsons (1), linebacker Edgerrin Cooper (56) and cornerback Keisean Nixon (25) team up to stop Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) on Sunday, September 7, 2025, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wis. The Packers won the game, 27-13. Tork Mason/USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin “Again, it’s going to be a process trying to get him back, but we’re hopeful. It’s going to be dependent upon the next couple days, but we’re hopeful he’ll be able to get out there sometime this week,” head coach Matt LaFleur commented. Green Bay is expected to be cautious with Micah Parsons as he works toward a return. Given the severity of his knee injury, the coaching staff does not want to rush him back or put unnecessary strain on his recovery. Once Parsons begins practicing, the Packers will have a 21-day window to move him from the Physically Unable to Perform list to the active roster. item.title: NBA makes Draymond Green decision after ejection vs Suns
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Another Draymond Green ejection, another familiar wave of fans waiting to see if the league will actually punish him. Draymond Green found another way to lose his cool, getting ejected after taking Khaman Maluach down and getting into an altercation with Dillon Brooks in the aftermath. It’s the same old story for Green, whose career has been defined by cheap shots, technicals, and suspensions that previously forced him into league-mandated therapy just to get back on the floor. And Brooks didn’t hold back postgame, claiming he only stepped in to de-escalate because Draymond had been acting up all game. Draymond Green to face no further action from NBA Dropping in on The Pat McAfee Show, Shams Charania gave everyone the definitive word: the NBA isn’t hitting Draymond Green with another suspension. He said: “I don’t expect the NBA to discipline Draymond Green any further for this play right here… but Draymond clearly got his l*** in right there.” Draymond caught a serious break here. With his rap sheet, he’s lucky the league didn’t throw the book at him. Sure, that chaotic energy might get the guys hyped, but Golden State is playing with fire. Pulling stunts like this will eventually cost the Warriors a game that actually counts. item.title: “It blew me away”: Pat Murphy reflects on Brewers’ championship parade
item.description: Pat Murphy and the Milwaukee Brewers have spent the past week enjoying the celebrations that followed their World Series victory. Players and staff attended Thursday night’s Green Bay Packers game, made appearances on programs including Saturday Night Live, and took part in a championship parade on Friday. On Tuesday, Murphy looked back on the festivities during an appearance on MLB Network. “It blew me away,” commented the Brewers manager. "They were just there to support the @Brewers . Bringing everybody together and the joy it spread, you felt it. Amazing turnout." – Pat Murphy on the World Series parade #MLBNHotStove | @SageUSAmerica pic.twitter.com/sWSETBBT5i — MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) November 3, 2026 “700,000 people they said. They were just there to support the Brewers, and how happy, bringing everybody together. And seeing the joy that it spread what our guys did to win that championship. That just did so much for our community, for our state.” Pat Murphy and the Brewers’ first World Series Oct 30, 2026; Milwaukee, WI, USA; Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy holds the Commissioner’s Trophy during the celebration of winning the World Series at Henry Maier Festival Park. Milwaukee will now look to build on its championship success and establish itself as a dynasty. Several key players are already under contract for multiple seasons, giving the Brewers a foundation to remain competitive. With much of the roster expected to stay together, another trip to the World Series could be within reach in the coming years. item.title: Manchester United 3-2 Roma: Cunha shines as Red Devils produce remarkable Champions League comeback
item.description: Manchester United 3-2 Roma: Cunha shines as Red Devils produce remarkable Champions League comeback Manchester United completed a magical comeback after being two goals down in the first half against Roma to give Michael Carrick a lifeline, with Matheus Cunha scoring twice before being sent off. Roma took quick-fire action in the first half, as Argentinian forward Matias Soulé’s low driven shot flew past Senne Lammens, before Donyell Malen sent the Belgian goalkeeper the wrong way to make it two early and mute Old Trafford. Manchester United flipped the game in the second half, as they had a penalty of their own when Matheus Cunha was fouled in the box, which was converted by captain Bruno Fernandes. The Brazilian forward’s footprint was all over the comeback with a brace, firstly scoring where he capitalised on Balerdi’s failure to clear the ball to convert from close range, and then a thunderous strike to beat Devis Vásquez in style, scoring an 83rd-minute winner. Despite the winner, two yellow cards in quick succession from the scorer of the winner had him dismissed in the closing minutes of the game. Yet Carrick’s men held out from Roma’s pressure to secure a very important win to end their nine-game winless streak and three points in the Champions League league phase to climb up to 17th. As it happened Before kick-off, a minute of silence was held in tribute to the tragic death of CD Tenerife footballer Jesús De Miguel following a collision during a match against Andorra. Manchester United’s defence were pierced through just 11 minutes into the game after Kobbie Mainoo was dispossessed in the midfield, before Portuguese teenager Rodrigo Mora found Matías Soulé through a measured diagonal ball in acres of space to set himself and coolly convert past Senne Lammens to silence Old Trafford. It was an absolute disaster for Michael Carrick’s side five minutes later when they conceded a penalty due to the ball hitting Ayden Heaven’s arm, blocking Soulé’s shot from the same area as his first unmarked goal. Donyell Malen’s red-hot form continued this season with eight goals in Serie A as he made it his fourth goal in the Champions League with a composed penalty to send the Belgian goalkeeper the wrong way and extend their lead by two. Although the home side tried to get back into the game in the first half, they lacked real quality in the final ball and action. When the whistle blew for half-time, boos rang around the stadium, conveying the dissatisfied, angry state the Mancunian supporters are in this season. At the start of the second-half, Manchester United were finally able to open up the Roma defence as Carlos Baleba galloped through on goal. But just when he was about to cross the ball, he pulled up with a suspected hamstring injury, which ironically summed up United’s situation, as Youri Tielemans was substituted on for the Cameroonian. item.title: Dodgers notes: Tarik Skubal, Shohei Ohtani
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Tarik Skubal #29 of the Los Angeles Dodgers throws a pitch against the Milwaukee Brewers during the first inning in game one of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 11, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Free agency has officially begun, and the Dodgers are now on the clock to try to fortify their roster before the impending lockout. Left-hander Tarik Skubal is atop the list of the most highly coveted free agents this offseason, and the Dodgers are not the only bidder for his services. Jeff Passan at ESPN reports that the New York Mets will compete with the Dodgers for the highest offer, while the Chicago Cubs want Skubal “badly.” The two most obvious suitors are the two teams with the highest payrolls in baseball: The Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets. There are bound to be others. The Chicago Cubs badly want Skubal. They also are skeptical that they will be willing to compete at the sort of dollars Skubal is expected to get — well in excess of $300 million, potentially in the $400 million-plus range. Alden Gonzalez of ESPN is more optimistic about the chances of Skubal returning to Los Angeles for 2027 and beyond. He truly seemed to relish his 2½ months in Los Angeles. He loved the culture, particularly being among so many established, veteran players who were singularly focused on winning. He became besties with Blake Snell, was awed by the organization’s resources and, overall, seemed to fit in seamlessly. Buster Olney of ESPN shared his thoughts on what type of deal Skubal is projected for, noting that a deal for him would resemble Kyle Tucker’s current deal with the Dodgers compared to Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s record setting deal. After two fantastic years of Shohei Ohtani in Dodger blue, the two-way superstar and still reigning two-time NL MVP award winner mired in a power drought in the second half and beyond that rendered him obsolete in the starting lineup. That was until he hit a towering three-run home run that gave the Dodgers their final runs of the 2026 postseason. David Adler of MLB.com notes that Ohtani’s Game 4 home run in the NLCS could help him get back on track hitting-wise before the start of the 2027 season. When we’re seeing Ohtani connect with the baseball with bat speeds like that, we know his swing is in the right place. Are we overanalyzing one home run? Maybe! But we think that one home run was a harbinger of what’s coming next year: the return of MVP-level Ohtani.

item.title: NFL Gross Quarterback Ranks: What do we think about Michael Penix Jr.?
item.description: How much stock can you put in a quarterback stuck in a constant downpour? That's the question NFL fans are asking after Michael Penix Jr. continued his roller coaster career with a gruesome performance in swampy Tampa Bay. Penix had more interceptions Sunday than the Buccaneers had pass attempts, clearing the way for him to surge to the top of this week's Gross Quarterback Rankings. But at least he can blame the weather. Jacoby Brissett, on the other hand, was playing the league's worst defense in a dome. There's no perfect metric for a quarterback's impact, but expected points added (EPA) helps measure their ability to swing the outcome of a game through the air, on the ground and through avoiding negative plays. Last year, EPA told us Drake Maye and Matthew Stafford were a cut above the rest of the league's quarterbacks in the regular season, netting 151.3 and 120.3 EPA , respectfully. No one else in the league topped triple digits. Unsurprisingly, those two led playoff teams and finished second and first, respectively, in MVP voting. We can use EPA to help dissect which quarterbacks underwhelmed the hardest in their debut. By comparing their Week 8 EPA across their early 2026 season averages, we get a better idea of whose fans should be most annoyed. And so, we end up with a "worst QBs" list that doesn't include Cam Ward or even Bo Nix, simply because their starts to the season have been so disappointing we've been moderately conditioned not to expect more this fall. You have to be at least decent in 2026 — or otherworldly awful on a given week — to wind up in the gross QB rankings. We'll also look at completion percentage over expected (CPOE), which gives you a good idea of which quarterbacks are making tough throws (and, in some cases, being bailed out by exceptional catches). All data come from NFL Pro. We'll also keep a running tally of the times each quarterback lands here. item.title: The second act nobody saw coming: Steven Alker's remarkable rise at 50
item.description: Five years ago, on a warm practice day at the PGA Tour Champions' Furyk & Friends tournament in Jacksonville, Florida, an unassuming New Zealander named Steven Alker was quietly working on the driving range. Few spectators stopped to watch. Fewer still could have imagined what was about to unfold. But one man saw something special. John Felice, a volunteer from Ponte Vedra Beach working the range, stood alongside a reporter and pointed toward Alker. "You need to watch this guy," he said. "He's got the most beautiful swing." The prediction proved remarkably prophetic. Alker was a journeyman At the time, Alker hardly appeared destined for stardom. He was a journeyman professional who had spent decades grinding through the highs and lows of a game that rarely rewards persistence. He chased opportunities around the globe, trying to carve out a living while remaining largely anonymous to golf fans. Meanwhile, the reporter was occupied tracking down more recognizable names such as quote machines Rocco Mediate and Paul Goydos, players who would eventually finish somewhere around 40th that week. Alker barely registered on anyone's radar. That was about to change. Making his way originally as a Monday qualifier, he finished tied for seventh, extending a remarkable streak of six consecutive top-10 finishes that season. Less than a month later, he captured his first PGA Tour Champions title, launching one of the most remarkable late-career renaissances in professional golf. For Scott McCarron, Alker's rise remains difficult to comprehend. "We all just wonder, where was he 20 years ago, you know what I mean?" McCarron said. It's a fair question. Alker's PGA Tour career was unspectacular In 87 career starts on the PGA Tour, Alker never recorded a top-10 finish. He earned less than $1 million competing against the world's best players and appeared destined to remain one of professional golf's forgettable names. Yet golf has a way of offering second chances, and Alker has taken full advantage of golf’s ultimate mulligan at age 50. The New Zealander has become one of the most successful unsung players in PGA Tour Champions history. He won the 2023 Charles Schwab Cup , has amassed 14 victories on the senior circuit and continues to perform at a level few could have imagined during his PGA Tour years. Now 55, he's showing little sign of slowing down. Alker recorded four victories and 12 top-10 finishes this season while pushing his PGA Tour Champions career earnings beyond $15 million. He enters this week's Charles Schwab Cup Championship in Phoenix ranked third in the standings. The formula, according to his peers, isn't complicated. It's execution. "He possesses one of the soundest swings on Tour, and he's a great putter," McCarron said. "Once he learned how to win, there was no stopping the guy. He has no weaknesses." item.title: No Bones About It: Hyland’s Stats Show He’s Stepping Up With Edwards Out
item.description: Nov 2, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard Bones Hyland (8) works around Milwaukee Bucks center Jericho Sims (00) in the first quarter at Target Center. Mandatory Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Benjamin Yu, Editor It was obvious that the Timberwolves needed someone to step up in the wake of Anthony Edwards ‘ knee injury. But it wasn’t obvious that it would be Bones Hyland . Hyland was barely playing before Edwards’ injury , and he’s still not getting huge minutes. However, Hyland’s stats in the four games since Edwards went out show that he’s taking advantage of the minutes he does get and has raised his game perhaps as much as any of the Timberwolves. Edwards’ Injury Paved The Way For More Meaningful Minutes Hyland struggled to crack coach Chris Finch’s regular rotation at the start of the season, which was a bit surprising. He was a valuable contributor off the bench last year, particularly after the Timberwolves traded for Ayo Dosunmu and the two earned the nickname “ Twin Turbos ” with their fast-paced play. Hyland started this season as the fifth player off the bench and was largely relegated to mop-up duty in the four games before Edwards’ injury. The only exception was a 117-94 win against Toronto, where Hyland played 15 minutes. He was great defensively in that game, notching three blocks and two steals. But he shot 0-5. In the four games since Edwards’ injury, Hyland’s has been thrust into the regular rotation and is averaging 16 meaningful minutes per game. Increased production has followed. Hyland’s Stats Are Way Up Based On Volume Bones had a total of nine points and four assists in the four games before Edwards went out. He’s averaging 12.0 points and 4.25 assists per game in the four games since. The highlight was a 19-point, eight-assist performance in a win over the Los Angeles Clippers, but Hyland hasn’t been a one-game wonder. He scored in double figures in three of the last four contests. It’s perhaps not surprising that with more minutes, Hyland is scoring more and dishing out more assists. But the impressive thing is that he’s doing it without sacrificing any efficiency. item.title: Every player from Arizona to play for the Boston Celtics - Jerryd Bayless
item.description: The Boston Celtics have traded for, signed, and drafted players from nearly every U.S. state and countries across the globe. From Alabama to Yugoslavia, the Celtics have a history of thoroughly seeking talent to succeed in the NBA. Since their beginnings in the Basketball Association of America (a precursor league of the NBA) in the earliest years of the Association, the organization has tirelessly searched for talent since its inception. In this installment of our series documenting the origins of every player who has represented the Celtics, we will focus on players from Arizona who have played for Boston. item.title: Kevin Durant shares what he thinks would be different about Shaquille O’Neal if he played in the NBA today
item.description: Photo by Don EMMERT / AFP via Getty Images Two-time NBA champion Kevin Durant believes that Shaquille O’Neal would continue to fill the stat sheet if he played in this era. Having won four championships in his career, Shaquille O’Neal retired as one of the most dominant players in the league. His strength and athleticism made it almost impossible to guard him, especially when he was playing alongside Kobe Bryant during his LA Lakers tenure. While discussing O’Neal’s game, the one thing that gets scrutinised is his inability to shoot the ball. However, Durant believes his dominance in the paint and passing as a big would allow the center to do so much even in today’s NBA. Kevin Durant feels Shaquille O’Neal would have way more space if he played in this era During the early 2000s, teams were not shooting much from the three-point line. In fact, during the 1999-2000 season, the average for three-pointers taken around the league was 13.7. This has now increased to 37.8 in the current season, which indicates how different the game is in the current era. However, Durant believes this would prove to be advantageous for the three-time Finals MVP, purely because of how dominant he was on the court. “I feel like it’s way more space for Shaq to operate, there’s way more skilled players, so he doesn’t have to do as much… Shaq would be getting triple-doubles, he would be getting more rebounds and he would score more points,” said Durant on The Rushmore podcast. Durant made this point about O’Neal while arguing that the current era of basketball is the best ever in the NBA. “There’s more shots going up, so more rebounds and there’s more shooters, so you could pass out of double teams. You could pass pretty well big fella, but he was passing to guys who couldn’t really shoot that well,” Durant added. The 54-year-old averaged 23.7 points and 10.9 rebounds for his career on 58.2% shooting from the field. While a big in today’s NBA is expected to shoot well, O’Neal made only 1 three-pointer throughout his career. If he played in today’s game, O’Neal would definitely have a lot of free throws, but even his shooting from the charity stripe was below average. However, his dominance in the paint alone would unlock the team’s offence. Alongside his offensive game, O’Neal was also brilliant on the defensive side of the game, averaging 2.3 blocks for his career. With him inside the paint, it would be difficult to imagine teams attacking the rim, as his presence alone would make things significantly harder. All these factors do make it clear that while O’Neal’s game is old-school, the way he played it would translate in any era of the league, which is why he will always be one of the best bigs the NBA has ever seen. item.title: Agent of veteran NFL coach shares whether Jerry Jones has contacted over Cowboys opportunity
item.description: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images Jerry Jones has admitted he is not looking to move on from Brian Schottenheimer despite the Dallas Cowboys’ dreadful start to the season. The Cowboys suffered yet another defeat at AT&T Stadium on Sunday. This time, America’s team lost to the Arizona Cardinals and it was clear to see just how frustrated the result left Jones as the broadcast cameras captured his reaction. Dallas head into this weekend sitting in second spot of the NFC East but their 3-5 record leaves a lot to be desired. Playing the Indianapolis Colts this weekend will provide Schottenheimer with a massive opportunity to get a win under his belt. Despite what many analysts may be saying, Jones is not yet looking to replace Schottenheimer, and the agent of one veteran NFL coach has expressed the reason why that might be. What an agent of one veteran NFL coach has said about Jerry Jones One of the biggest issues Jones has suffered from over the years is not wanting to spend big on coaching staff. This has not been an issue for Jones when it comes to players, but he has often looked to find a bargain with his coaches. ESPN reporter Jane Slater shared the response she received from the agent of one veteran coach after she asked around about Jones potentially moving on from Schottenheimer. “I called the agent of a veteran coach to see if Jerry Jones had even picked up the phone and poked around on him during the Schottenheimer hiring cycle and he laughed and said “Jerry won’t pay 13M and up and that’s the starting point” It’s well known and well documented just surprised he actually finally said it on record today,” she said on X. It feels as if something has to change for the Cowboys to truly make a step in the right direction. The finances and belief have been shown by Jones in trying to improve the roster but it seems as if the coaching may still be holding the Cowboys back. However, Cowboys fans will also feel as if they have been saying this for decades, with their last Super Bowl trophy coming all the way back in 1996. If Schottenheimer cannot secure a win over the Colts, then it is hard to see how he could continue as the head coach. item.title: The LeBron James stat that shows why the Philadelphia 76ers are bound for the NBA Finals
item.description: Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images The Philadelphia 76ers fans are already looking forward to a run to the 2027 NBA Finals after one specific LeBron James stat proves to be a major indicator. The 76ers are leading the Eastern Conference after the first two weeks of the 2026-27 NBA season, holding a 7-1 record with the team looking comfortable as the leading contenders in the East. The additions of LeBron and Jaylen Brown have been a major factor in enabling this success, with LeBron in particular bringing 23 years of experience with 10 Finals appearances and four championships. LeBron James’ career trend indicates the 76ers are NBA Finals-bound As mentioned, James has made the NBA Finals 10 times over his career. Every single time his team has started the season 7-1 (4 instances), they have invariably reached the Finals , with three NBA Championships being won in the process. LeBron led the 11-12 Heat, 15-16 Cavaliers, 16-17 Cavaliers, and 19-20 Lakers all to 7-1 starts in those respective seasons. Outside the 16-17 Cavaliers, each squad won the NBA title, with the 16-17 Cavaliers losing to the Golden State Warriors with Kevin Durant. If this career trend from James is to be held, the 76ers are bound to reach the NBA Finals in 2027. So far, they do look like the favourites to do so, with their closest rivals being the 6-1 Detroit Pistons, who still have roster flaws to work through. The 5-2 Boston Celtics are interesting opponents but might struggle to match up with the depth and talent of the 76ers, while other presumed contenders such as the 4-2 Toronto Raptors and 3-4 New York Knicks have had spotty starts to the season. If the trend of LeBron’s 7-1 teams going to the NBA Finals is to be broken, one of the East’s elites need to step up and stop the 76ers, who are looking like a well-organised machine far quicker than most anticipated. James is playing the perfect team-first role, averaging 16.2 points, 7.3 assists and 7.0 rebounds while playing some of the best defence we have seen from him in the last five years. But although the analogy holds some truth, over the first two seasons of the team's existence, the Valkyries' home court has come to mean much more to many of their fans than just supporting a basketball team. "I've said it multiple times that Ballhalla became my safe space," said Golden State Valkyries star Gabby Williams in an end-of-season exit interview where she noted that she received death threats for her support of transgender rights. Valkyries fans shut them down. Full Valkyries coverage For all of our Bay Area sports coverage, sign up for The Catch newsletter . One of the rallying cries for fans happened after the Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream on Pride Night on June 26. Williams found a camera on the court and yelled : "For the gays!" Many Valkyries fans, including a sizable queer presence, felt connected to the team that represented and brought joy to the San Francisco Bay Area. item.title: Villanova has 20 reasons to feel better about its season-opening loss
item.description: Oh mio Dio! Villanova basketball’s trip to Rome for the Eternal City Tip-Off didn’t exactly end the way Wildcat fans had hoped. The Cats opened their 2026-27 season with a frustrating 74-72 loss to former Big East rival Notre Dame on Sunday, blowing a 10-point second-half lead in a game they probably should’ve won comfortably. But there’s a pretty good reason to feel optimistic about Kevin Willard’s squad after its first game. Actually, there are 20 of them. Nova turned the ball over 20 times against the Fighting Irish, including an almost-impressive 15 giveaways in the first half alone. The Irish turned those mistakes into 20 points, which is a pretty good way to lose a basketball game you otherwise controlled. And somehow, the turnovers weren’t the only problem. The Wildcats also surrendered 17 offensive rebounds, giving Notre Dame second and third chances on possessions that should’ve gone the other way. Between the turnovers and their inability to clean up the glass, Villanova essentially handed the Irish enough extra opportunities to steal a game they had little business winning. Here’s the encouraging part. Villanova shot 46.2% from the field compared to Notre Dame’s 35.4%. Willard’s squad made more shots despite attempting 13 fewer, held the lead for 83% of the game and looked like the better team for most of the afternoon. That’s pretty encouraging for a team still figuring out how to play together. Of course, nobody should be celebrating 20 turnovers or pretending the rebounding issues will magically fix themselves. Willard has plenty to clean up before Friday’s home opener against Holy Cross. But the Wildcats also cut their turnovers from 15 in the first half to five in the second, which suggests some of the sloppiness can be corrected as this group gets more comfortable playing together. It’s Game 1. There are going to be growing pains, especially with a roster that’s almost entirely new. Villanova already showed it can do everything else that’s required for a win. Taking better care of the basketball and finishing defensive possessions would go a long way toward turning those encouraging stretches of “what’s required to win” into actual wins. The loss stinks, especially considering it was against Notre Lame (ha(!), got em). But if Willard can clean up those two areas, there’s plenty to like about what the Wildcats showed in Italy.

item.title: Promising Waldemar Anton update in Germany gives Man United the final motivation to seal transfer
item.description: Promising Waldemar Anton update in Germany gives Man United the final motivation to seal transfer Come 2027, defensive signings will sit firmly at the top of Manchester United’s agenda. After overhauling the attack and midfield over the last two summer windows, the club plans to build a formidable backline next year. In doing so, the Red Devils must recruit quality defenders who can arrive and make an immediate impact. One such defender is Borussia Dortmund’s Waldemar Anton . The versatile centre-back, who can also operate at right-back, has long been of interest to United. Why Waldemar Anton United view him as an imposing, no-nonsense centre-back. They hope to capitalise on his strength in aerial duels and ground battles, as well as his sharp reading of the game—traits the club believes will suit the intensity of the Premier League. Beyond that, he is regarded as a “silent leader” in the Dortmund dressing room, bringing experience, organisation, and composure under pressure. He could therefore serve as a valuable role model for young defenders such as Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro. All that said, if the Red Devils needed any extra motivation to act on their interest in Anton, they have it now thanks to the latest reports emerging from Germany. Massive boost from Germany Sport Bild, as cited by Buli News , claims: “Dortmund are looking to tie Waldemar Anton down to a contract beyond 2028, but negotiations are seemingly proving more difficult than initially anticipated.” They explain: “Talks between the two parties have been progressing slowly, and a swift agreement is not in sight because the proposed salary doesn’t meet the player’s expectations.” These tricky contract-extension talks should certainly boost United’s chances of landing Anton. INEOS ought to move decisively, turning his head with a strong offer and the promise of a key role. Such an approach could persuade him to snub Dortmund’s extension offers entirely and allow United to snap him up at a bargain next year. With Lisandro Martínez likely to leave amid interest from Barcelona , replacing his quality, experience, and leadership with Anton’s could prove a genuine transfer masterstroke. item.description: A win is a win, and Michigan left Piscataway with one over Rutgers in the worst game for the Wolverines’ defense so far this season. After not allowing more than 20 points in a game through seven games, it was Rutgers of all teams that broke that streak. And while the offense showed some encouraging signs with freshman quarterback Tommy Carr, there are still plenty of questions heading into one of the most important games of the season against Michigan State — no matter what the Spartans’ record says. The Paul Bunyan Trophy is up for grabs this weekend, and Michigan — and its coaching staff, specifically — can’t afford to overlook its in-state rival. Fact: Jason Beck’s seat is still incredibly hot One Carr flu game isn’t going to be enough for Michigan fans to shy away from calling for offensive coordinator Jason Beck’s head. The Wolverines scored their most points in a conference game this season last week, but the offense still ranks 127th in total offense and second-last in the Big Ten in passing offense. Much of Michigan’s success came from the creativity of Carr to escape the pocket and take off. The run game still struggled as a collective, running for a little more than three yards per carry despite Savion Hiter logging 76 yards on 20 carries. The offensive line is still being shuffled around due to injury and can’t seem to find a rhythm. Beck still has much to figure out and not much time to do so. Michigan State also boasts one of the worst offenses in all of the FBS, but the Spartans’ defense is not nearly as bad as Rutgers. Michigan State is at 50th in yards allowed per game and 66th in points allowed per game. If the Spartans somehow find a way to win a low-scoring slugfest, it could be the end of the line for Beck.
